preconditions.description: Input constraints for n (stations), m (two-way railways), and q (incidents) are satisfied.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= w_i <= 10**9 for w_i in w) and len(w) == n
preconditions.description: Each station's construction cost w_i is a positive integer within bounds, and there are exactly n costs.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= u <= n and 1 <= v <= n and u != v and 1 <= d <= 10**9 for u, v, d in railways) and len(railways) == m
preconditions.description: Each two-way railway connects distinct stations with a positive integer length, and there are exactly m railways.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= k_i <= n and 1 <= x_i <= 4 * 10**8 for k_i, x_i in incidents) and len(incidents) == q
preconditions.description: Each incident updates the cost of building from station k_i by adding x_i, and there are exactly q incidents.
The two-way railways form a connected graph (any station reachable from any other).

postconditions.description: Output contains exactly q+1 lines, one for each state (initial and after each incident).

postconditions.expression: all(is_valid_solution(w, railways, incidents[:i], output_lines[i]) for i in range(q + 1))
postconditions.description: For each state (initial and after each incident), the output is the minimal cost of constructing one-way railways such that: (1) there are at least two shortest paths from station 1 to any other station, (2) these paths share no common stations except station 1 and the terminal, and (3) the shortest path distances from station 1 to any other station remain unchanged.
